questions: Who does most of the cooking in your home?
What is a dish that you can cook well?
Do you prefer eating at home or eating out?
Has your taste in food changed since you were a child?

teaching.tense_focus: present simple for habits, present perfect for how your taste has changed
teaching.band_move: Name the dish. Food questions are answered with nouns, and a specific dish is worth more than any adjective.

questions.answer_shape: Say how much, name what you enjoy or hate about it, then when you do it.
questions.extend_move: I do when there's no rush — it's cooking on a Tuesday at seven that I resent.

common_error.wrong: I enjoy to cook at the weekend.
common_error.right: I enjoy cooking at the weekend.

questions.answer_shape: Name who, say how that was decided, then what you contribute.
questions.extend_move: My partner does, mainly because he's faster and I'm the one who clears up.

common_error.wrong: My mother makes the most of cooking.
common_error.right: My mother does most of the cooking.
common_error.why: You 'do' the cooking; 'make the most of' means something else.

questions.probe: Has that always been the case?

questions.answer_shape: Name the dish, say where you learned it, then who you cook it for.
questions.extend_move: A lentil soup my grandmother made — six ingredients and almost impossible to ruin.

common_error.wrong: I can cook well the rice.
common_error.why: The adverb follows the object, and 'rice' takes no article.

questions.answer_shape: Choose one, name what each gives you, then say when you'd swap.
questions.extend_move: At home, mostly — eating out is fine, but I resent paying for something I could make.

common_error.wrong: I prefer eat at home than in restaurant.
common_error.right: I prefer eating at home to eating out.
common_error.why: After 'prefer', use -ing, and link the two options with 'to'.

questions.probe: How often do you eat out?

questions.answer_shape: Say what changed, name one food you now like, then one you have given up.
questions.extend_move: Enormously — I wouldn't touch anything bitter as a child and now I live on coffee and olives.

common_error.wrong: My taste is changed since I am a child.
common_error.right: My taste has changed since I was a child.
common_error.why: 'Since' plus a past point takes present perfect and past simple.
